method: E06-full: 20 hand-labeled routing scenarios (experiments/e06-scenarios.txt), grader prompts in experiments/e06-grader-*.md, 2 runs per model via hermes chat --format stream-json, strict N: route parsing, accuracy vs hand labels in results/e06-labels.json
verdict: Verdict: On 20 hand-labeled routing scenarios x 2 runs, gpt-6-luna scored 0.675 mean accuracy vs deepseek-v4-flash's 0.650 — a 1-item difference, well within run-to-run noise, and 10 of the 12 combined misses are the SAME five ambiguous 'trivial-but-constructive' items (cron-debug+patch, inbox summarize, tweet draft, typo fix, CSV convert) where both models reasonably say 'default' but the label says 'none', plus two advisor/default boundary cases. Neither model actually disagrees with the other in any meaningful way; the ceiling here is label quality, not model quality. However, luna is ALSO cheaper in practice: its harness input is prompt-cached (~3-6 billed input tokens per run), while deepseek's verbatim-first-run 14k input and 1.5-2x output verbosity put its real cost per pass (~$0.00085) ~7x luna's (~$0.00012). Conclusion: do NOT switch routing to deepseek-v4-flash on accuracy grounds — it shows no advantage and costs more in practice; luna's ~3-5x list-price gap is irrelevant at this volume (<$0.001/pass), so the current luna pin stands. Recommended follow-up: re-run with tightened 'none' definitions (explicitly list 'small fix/draft/admin' examples) before any future router-model decision, since label ambiguity dominates the error budget.
